questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The total mechanical energy of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is proportional to:
questions.explanation: E = ½mω²A², so the energy depends on A² and stays constant through the motion even though kinetic and potential energy keep interchanging.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The quantity of heat needed to change 1 kg of ice at 0 °C into water at 0 °C is called its:
questions.explanation: During melting the temperature does not change because the heat supplied, about 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ for ice, goes into breaking the bonds of the solid.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 10: Thermal Properties of Matter

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is taken as:
questions.explanation: A normal eye can focus comfortably on objects from 25 cm up to infinity. This 25 cm value is used in the magnifying power formulas of a lens and a microscope.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in excess oxygen is called the enthalpy of:
questions.explanation: Enthalpy of combustion is always negative because burning releases heat, and it is the quantity measured in a bomb calorimeter.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, the product obtained at the cathode is:
questions.explanation: Reduction occurs at the cathode, so Na⁺ gains an electron to give sodium metal, while Cl⁻ is oxidised to chlorine at the anode. With aqueous NaCl, hydrogen appears instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question: Which of the following compounds can show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: Geometrical isomerism needs restricted rotation about a double bond and two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon. Only but-2-ene satisfies both conditions here.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 8: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of the genetic code?
questions.explanation: The code is unambiguous: one codon always specifies only one amino acid. It is degenerate because several codons may code for the same amino acid.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: RNA interference has been used to develop transgenic tobacco plants resistant to:
questions.explanation: Introducing both sense and antisense RNA creates double stranded RNA that silences the parasite's gene, so the nematode cannot survive in the transgenic host.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Inside the seminiferous tubules, the cells that nourish and support the developing germ cells are:
questions.explanation: Sertoli or nurse cells provide nutrition to the germ cells, while the interstitial Leydig cells outside the tubules secrete androgens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which class of vertebrates has a three chambered heart in all its members except the crocodile?
questions.explanation: Reptiles have two atria and an incompletely divided ventricle, but the crocodile is an exception with a four chambered heart. Birds and mammals always have four chambers.
